title: Democracy, Civil Society and the Media
summary: The role of civil society organisations in a democracy, the media as a watchdog, freedom of the press and its limits, responsible media use, and youth participation in community and national issues.

notes.text: Organisations and groups outside government and business that represent the interests of citizens: NGOs, community-based organisations, trade unions, faith groups, student and youth organisations.

rows: Access to HIV treatment and health services

items: It gives a **voice** to people who might be ignored.
It provides **services** (care, food, education) where needed.
It can take issues to **court**, e.g. TAC's case that led to the national programme to prevent mother-to-child transmission of HIV.

notes.text: Section 16 of the Constitution protects **freedom of expression**, including freedom of the press. The media **inform** the public, **expose** wrongdoing (the watchdog role), and allow **debate**. Freedom of expression is limited: it excludes propaganda for war, incitement of imminent violence and hate speech.

notes.label: Responsible media use
notes.text: Check sources before sharing, recognise bias and fake news, respect others' privacy and dignity online, and remember that posts can have legal consequences (defamation, the Cybercrimes Act).

items: Join school governing bodies (as RCL members), youth councils and community forums.
Volunteer with NGOs or start a campaign on an issue you care about.
Use social media responsibly to raise awareness and mobilise peacefully.
Remember **16 June** (Youth Day): young people have shaped South Africa's history.
